courses.title: Elementary Japanese (First Quarter)
courses.description: This course offers an introduction to the Japanese language and culture, with a focus on language as both a primary expression of culture and a medium of communication. Students will develop the four essential language skills—listening, speaking, reading, and writing—along with sociocultural knowledge that is vital for effective communication in Japanese. Japanese will be the primary language of instruction. Oral practice will be emphasized and supported by a foundational understanding of language structures. Students are expected to master two of the Japanese syllabic writing systems, hiragana and katakana, as well as 29 kanji (Chinese characters).
courses.advisories: ESL D272. and ESL D273., or ESL D472. and ESL D473., or eligibility for ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Demonstrate a working command of essential vocabulary and language structures necessary to request and provide, orally and in writing, basic/simple information relating to high-frequency situations in familiar contexts such as greetings, introductions, school, dating, and invitations. This includes recognizing and reproducing 46 Japanese syllable-based Hiragana and Katakana characters, as well as 29 Kanji Chinese characters. Distinguish meaning from short, simple texts on familiar topics, relying on contextual clues to extract the gist and some detail. Compose comprehensible, simple phrases or sentences about familiar topics to reflect a working commnad of core vocabulary and language structures. Demonstrate a cursory grasp of social protocols and contributions of Japanese culture, by analyzing and comparing them to one's own cultures.

courses.title: Elementary Japanese (Second Quarter)
courses.description: This course is a continuation of the introduction to the Japanese language and culture. Emphasis will be placed on developing beginner-level proficiency appropriate for the second quarter in the four language skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Students will also deepen their understanding of sociocultural knowledge, which plays a crucial role in effective communication in Japanese. Japanese will remain the primary language of instruction. Oral practice will be emphasized and supported by a growing understanding of language structures. In addition to continued practice with the two Japanese syllabic writing systems, hiragana and katakana, students will review the initial 29 kanji (Sino-Japanese characters) and learn 57 additional kanji.
courses.prerequisites: JAPN D001. (equivalent to one year of high school Japanese) or equivalent
courses.advisories: ESL D272. and ESL D273., or ESL D472. and ESL D473., or eligibility for ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

courses.title: Elementary Japanese (Third Quarter)
courses.description: This course continues the introduction to the Japanese language and culture, building on previously acquired skills and knowledge. Emphasis will be placed on developing high-beginner proficiency in the four core language skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Students will also expand their understanding of sociocultural concepts that are essential for effective communication in Japanese. Oral practice will be further emphasized, supported by a solid grasp of language structures. An additional 59 kanji (Sino-Japanese characters) will be introduced. Students are expected to integrate all three Japanese writing systems—hiragana, katakana, and kanji—to demonstrate increasingly authentic writing skills.

courses.title: Intermediate Japanese (First Quarter)
courses.description: This is the first quarter of Intermediate Japanese. The course focuses on developing low-intermediate proficiency in the four language skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Emphasis will also be placed on acquiring sociocultural knowledge essential for effective communication in Japanese. Oral practice will build upon an understanding of language structures, which will be further reinforced throughout the course. Students will learn an additional 64 kanji (Sino-Japanese characters) and continue to integrate hiragana, katakana, and kanji in both reading and writing. Low-intermediate level reading strategies and writing skills will be introduced and practiced.

metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Compose comprehensible, paragraph-level discourse about familiar topics to reflect an increasingly consistent command of vocabulary and language structures. Demonstrate an increasingly accurate grasp of the subtleties in the idiosyncracies of Japanese culture, by analyzing and comparing them to one's own culture(s). Demonstrate increasing command of essential vocabulary and language structures, both orally and in writing, necessary to request and provide information. Recognize and reproduce an additional 64 kanji while engaging with a broader range of topics, including job searching, the Japanese banking system, annual events, travel to various cities, lost and found situations, and gift-giving customs in Japan. Distinguish meaning from longer texts of increasing complexity, [relying less on contextual clues] to extract main ideas and supporting details, and to interpret some subtleties of the text.

courses.title: Intermediate Japanese (Second Quarter)
courses.description: The second quarter of intermediate Japanese builds upon previously learned materials and focuses on further developing the four core language skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing. The course also deepens students’ understanding of sociocultural aspects that are essential for effective communication in Japanese. Emphasis will be placed on oral practice supported by a solid grasp of language structures. Students will be introduced to sixty-two additional kanji (Sino-Japanese characters) and will strengthen their reading strategies and writing skills by integrating hiragana, katakana, and kanji.

metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Compose extended, paragraph-level discourse about familiar topics to reflect a somewhat sustained command of vocabulary and language structures. Demonstrate a somewhat sustained command of vocabulary and language structures necessary to spontaneously request and provide information, both orally and in writing. Demonstrate a noticeably accurate grasp of the subtleties in the idiosyncracies of Japanese culture, by analyzing and comparing them to one's own culture(s). Recognize and reproduce an additional 62 kanji while engaging with a wider range of more sophisticated topics, such as the workplace, part-time jobs, sushi, visiting someone's home, and giving or understanding directions to various locations. Distinguish meaning from texts of greater sophistication, to interpret an expanding range of subtleties of the structure and content of the text.

courses.title: Intermediate Japanese (Third Quarter)
courses.description: This is the third quarter of intermediate Japanese. The course continues to develop students' proficiency in the Japanese language and understanding of Japanese culture, building on previously learned material. Emphasis will be placed on acquiring high-intermediate level skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing, as well as on expanding sociocultural knowledge essential for effective communication in Japanese. Oral practice will be emphasized and supported by a deeper understanding of language structures. An additional 46 kanji (Sino-Japanese characters) will be introduced. Students will also develop high-intermediate reading strategies and writing skills, integrating hiragana, katakana, and kanji.
